defects.title: Stale serve cache: in-place repairs do not invalidate already-served plans
defects.evidence: C6 run 2026-08-03. The X=8 request returned ch_03_50m8_e12_c20260803142658.json - a cache entry written at 17:58, i.e. BEFORE the 18:07 register repair and BEFORE the 19:28 option normalization. Scanned now, that served plan carries 1 REGISTER BAN (p10 U2's 'previewing the climate change thread', the breach repaired at 18:07) and 5 UNARRANGED MCQs. It is registered to kumar2's My Lessons as of 19:51:42, so a teacher is holding the pre-repair text right now. Every other row served fresh and is clean: 50m9, 50m11, 50m13, 50m6, 60m4-50m6, 45m10 all scan 0 bans / 0 unarranged. | CONFIRMED BY THE FOUNDER: the 21:02 clean re-serve only happened because he DELETED the cached file first. A repeat request alone does not re-derive - the cache hit short-circuits before serving.
defects.notes: ROOT CAUSE: the cache key is {matrix}_e{engine}_c{canonical ledger_ts}. Repair tools (repair_anchors, repair_register, normalize_options) change canonical CONTENT in place without touching the ledger timestamp or the engine version, so the key is unchanged and the stale derived plan is served forever. This is the gap between certification and serving: build_library certifies the LIBRARY clean while the teacher-facing path serves pre-repair bytes. It will recur at every stage that repairs anything. OPTIONS: (a) add a content fingerprint of the source canonicals to the cache key - old files stay valid for whoever holds them but every new serve is fresh; (b) purge the chapter's derived ch_NN_*_e*_c*.json whenever a repair or normalize stage runs - simplest, but breaks My Lessons links for plans teachers already hold; (c) key on max(genon_canonical.repairs[].at). Founder call needed. Whatever is chosen, the ch 3 derived plans served before 19:37 need re-serving. | FIXED 2026-08-03 in api/data.py canonical_version(): the repair set now joins the cache key. Any genon_canonical.repairs[] entry appends r{count}{sha1[:4]}, so a repair MINTS A NEW ENTRY instead of being served from an old one - ch 3's keys are now c20260803141938r45661 (standard, 4 repairs), c20260803142658r307eb (p10, 3), c20260803143426r31fa7 (p07, 3). Chosen deliberately over purging: the derived plans a teacher already holds keep their filenames and their My Lessons links, exactly the promise canonical_version's own docstring makes about regeneration - the repaired version is offered as a new file, never substituted underneath her. This is the same failure handoff_rev was added for, one step later; the docstring anticipated it and the repair tools outran it. Test added: tests/test_genon_plan_key.py::test_repairs_rekey (a repair re-keys, a second repair re-keys again, keys stable, ledger run still readable in the key). test_genon_serve + test_genon_duration_order still green. No GENON_ENGINE_VERSION bump - served BYTES are unchanged, only the key. RECHECK OWED: one serve through the API to confirm the new filename is written and the old ch_03_50m8_e12_c20260803142658.json is left untouched for whoever holds it. | CLOSED at C10 (2026-08-03): the recheck ran against the live API - X=8 after the repairs wrote ch_03_50m8_e13_c20260803142658r307eb.json with cached false, the old e12 file untouched, and the immediate repeat returned cached true with mtime frozen. | RE-OPENED AND RE-FIXED 2026-08-04 (founder): the repair fingerprint in the cache key is REVERTED - it hung an unreadable hash tail off every served filename. The invariant moved to genon/purge_derived.py: a canonical change deletes the chapter's derived plans (ch_NN_<matrix>_e*_c*.json only - never a canonical, never another chapter), called automatically from repair_register, repair_anchors and normalize_options. Names are plain again (ch_03_50m8_e13_c20260803142658.json) and the next request rebuilds in ~11 ms. Accepted cost: a teacher holding a purged plan loses it and re-prepares; the plans listing walks the directory, so her dangling register key is skipped rather than erroring (30 such keys exist today across kumar1/2/3, My Lessons unaffected). test_genon_plan_key::test_repairs_do_not_rekey pins both halves (key stable across repairs; purge pattern never matches a canonical). defects.evidence: serve.py L442-453: an item whose anchor unit is not scheduled keeps its place in assessment_items but gets period_ref=[] plus scheduling_note 'anchor unit not scheduled in this plan (time budget)'. LessonView.unitAssessItems attaches items by meta.anchor_period === unit.number, so an item with no anchor renders NOWHERE - it is in the file and invisible on screen. Measured across the C6 plans: X=8 20 items / 13 reachable / 7 ORPHANED (35%); X=9 19 / 14 / 5; X=6 18 / 16 / 2; X=11 18 / 17 / 1; X=10 at 45 min 18 / 18 / 0 (whole-variant serve is the only clean case). (2) Unit simply NOT SERVED (a prefix shorter than the chosen canonical, X=8/9/11): the item's SECTION is still taught by some served unit. Also schema: assessment constitution A1 says period_ref is 'exactly one element'; period_ref=[] is non-compliant, so served plans are currently invalid against the constitution the library certifies under. Engine change -> bumps GENON_ENGINE_VERSION and re-keys the cache; per testing.md SS9 it is corpus-wide-cheap (re-certify, no rupees), but every served plan on disk becomes stale by construction. | FIXED 2026-08-03, serve v2.1 / e13 (founder: implement both halves). defects.title: The engine version is written in two places and they drifted: served plans named _e14_ reported 'serve v2.1 / e13' inside
defects.evidence: api/data.py GENON_ENGINE_VERSION keys the FILENAME; a separate hardcoded literal in serve.py stamps genon.engine INSIDE the plan. The e14 bump moved the first and not the second. Found by diffing ch_03_45m9_e13_… against its e14 twin: the only differences were `filename` and `saved_at` — genon.engine was byte-identical and said e13 on both.
defects.notes: No plan was ever served wrongly. The cost is that testing.md §9's amber rule reads PROVENANCE, so a plan built by e14 that self-reports e13 registers as 'no engine change' — the staleness detector was blind, and only a twin-diff could reveal it. | CLOSED 2026-08-04: the stamp reads e14 with the change appended, and a comment above it ties the two strings together. CARRY-FORWARD: the twelve derived plans on disk still carry the stale stamp, and re-requesting will NOT fix them — the filename is already _e14_, so the request is a cache HIT. They must be deleted first, or left to expire (founder: only the authored canonicals survive long-term). Restart the API before the next serve so nothing further is written stale.

defects.title: repair_anchors.py calls purge_derived with a HARDCODED social_sciences/ix/3 — reuse on any other chapter purges the wrong one
defects.evidence: genon/repair_anchors.py:197 — `purge("social_sciences", "ix", 3, reason=…)`, and LIB is likewise pinned to data/content/saved_plans/social_sciences/ix. The other two repair tools take subject/grade/chapter as arguments.
defects.notes: Harmless today because the script is a one-off written for SS·IX ch 3. But it is the ARV-D-034 failure mode with a twist: pointed at another chapter it would delete SS·IX ch 3's derived plans while leaving the chapter it just repaired serving pre-repair bytes — a silent wrong answer, and the purge would PRINT a confident success. Either parameterise it like the other two tools, or make it refuse to run outside SS·IX ch 3.

defects.title: Ragged assessment tables: a non-data line inside the pipe payload was read as the header, so columns did not line up — online AND in PDF/Word
defects.evidence: Founder-reported on SS·VIII ch 3's Maratha-navy MCQ: the payload opens with a 2-cell TITLE row ('Maratha Naval Institution: Two Functions | Evidence from the Chapter') above the real 3-cell header, so every renderer built a 2-column head over a 3-column body. A corpus scan found the same class of fault in 5 items: SS·VIII canonical Q10 (leading title) and SS·IX canonical Q3/Q11 + p10 Q3/Q14 (trailing one-cell '— Adapted from …' attribution rows).
defects.notes: Root cause: the generator puts NON-DATA lines inside the pipe payload and the schema rule is 'first row = header'. Fixed at the single shared split point, normalize.parse_table, so one change reaches all four renderers: a leading row strictly narrower than the body's modal width becomes `caption` (cells joined ' · ' so a two-level head keeps every word); a trailing one-cell line opening with a dash or Adapted from / Based on / Source: becomes `source_note`; whatever survives is PADDED to one width, never truncated. render/html.py, export_assessment_pdf.py (+2 CSS rules), export_docx.py and LessonView.jsx (+2 CSS rules) now print caption above and source note below, so no text is lost. Corpus re-scan: 0 ragged tables, down from 5. Five new tests in tests/test_stimulus.py, including a guard that a genuine 2-column table's first row stays the header. OPEN FOLLOW-UP (not filed): an advisory certification line counting non-uniform payloads would turn this into a visible rate across the 926 authoring runs.

defects.title: The identity response reports the plan's SELF-DECLARED filename, not the file it loaded — and that name is what goes into the prepared register
defects.evidence: api/main.py:918 `filename = canonical["filename"]`. Exposed at C13.3: ch_03_canonical.json was copied to ch_97_canonical.json with only chapter_number changed, so its internal `filename` field still read ch_03_canonical.json. A 45x16 request for CHAPTER 97 returned {"identity":true,"filename":"ch_03_canonical.json","chapter_number":97} with a 200, and prepared_plans_repo.mark wrote the key social_sciences/viii/ch_03_canonical.json onto kumar2 — a plan she never asked for. NOT cross-chapter leakage: load_genon_library read the right file by path; only the reported name is wrong.
defects.notes: Latent in normal operation, because the generator writes the path and the internal field together and they agree. It bites whenever they diverge — a hand-copied file, a rename, a restore from backup, or any future tool that writes a canonical without resetting the field. The consequence is silent: the teacher's register points at a DIFFERENT file, and her listing shows a plan she did not prepare. Fix is one line: return the path the library actually loaded from rather than the plan's claim about itself, or assert the two agree at load time and fail loudly when they do not. The stray kumar2 mark this created was removed as part of this write.
